**Explanation (coaching note):**
When your opponent's king flees to the edge, it becomes vulnerable. Here, forcing Rh2+ drives White's king to h2. After it captures, Re2+ is a powerful follow-up—your rook checks while simultaneously attacking c2. White's king has nowhere safe to go, and on Kh3, your queen swoops in with Qxg4+, winning White's queen. The lesson: aggressive piece placement near an exposed king often creates forcing tactics that win material. Look for ways to drive kings toward the edge—they're weak there.
